title: Finite-cover scalar localization gives uniform power torsion
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and let $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be any object of the derived category of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$-modules. Let $\{U_j\to X\}_{j=1}^t$ be a finite covering in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and for each $j$ let $C|_{U_j}$ be the termwise restriction of $C$ to the slice $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_j$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], an object of the derived category $D_j$ of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}|_{U_j}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; $D_j$ is $\mathcal O_E$-linear. Suppose that for every $j$ the image of $C|_{U_j}$ in the scalar localization $D_j[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] is a zero object, equivalently that $\varpi_E^{N_j}\operatorname{id}_{C|_{U_j}}=0$ in $D_j$ for some $N_j\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Then there exists $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ such that $\varpi_E^N\mathcal H^d(C)=0$, as a sheaf of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$-modules, for every $d\in\mathbf Z$. The case $t=0$ is permitted when the empty family covers $X$.

proof.text: For each member of the finite covering, choose an exponent $N_j$ supplied by the hypothesis. If $t>0$, let $N=\max_{1\le j\le t}N_j$; if $t=0$, put $N=0$. For every $j$ we have $N\ge N_j$, and the $\mathcal O_E$-linear composition and scalar action in $D_j$ give $\varpi_E^N\operatorname{id}_{C|_{U_j}}=\varpi_E^{N-N_j}(\varpi_E^{N_j}\operatorname{id}_{C|_{U_j}})=0$.

proof.text: Restriction of sheaves of modules to a localized site is exact, so it preserves kernels, images and cokernels. Applying this to the cohomology formula gives a natural identification $\mathcal H^d(C|_{U_j})\cong(\mathcal H^d(C))|_{U_j}$. On complexes, the map induced by scalar multiplication on the quotient $\ker d^d/\operatorname{im}d^{d-1}$ is scalar multiplication by the same scalar. This identity persists on derived morphisms, since cohomology factors through quasi-isomorphism localization. Applying cohomology to Step 1 therefore gives $\varpi_E^N\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal H^d(C|_{U_j})}=0$. Exact restriction also preserves the image of scalar multiplication; consequently the image sheaf $(\varpi_E^N\mathcal H^d(C))|_{U_j}$ is zero for every $d$ and $j$.

proof.text: Fix $d$ and set $H=\operatorname{im}(\varpi_E^N\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal H^d(C)})$, the image in the abelian category of module sheaves. Step 2 says $H|_{U_j}=0$. Apply the cited cover-local criterion to the underlying abelian sheaf of $H$ and the morphism $0\to H$. Its covering hypothesis holds: for any object $V\to X$, the pullback family $V\times_X U_j\to V$ is a covering, and every domain admits a map to $U_j$. Thus the sieve of arrows to $V$ whose domains map to some $U_j$ contains this covering family and is covering. The restrictions of $0\to H$ are isomorphisms, so the criterion gives an isomorphism of underlying abelian sheaves globally. Hence $H$ is the zero module sheaf, which says $\varpi_E^N\mathcal H^d(C)=0$. The argument holds for every $d$ with the same $N$. If $t=0$, pullback stability gives the empty covering on every $V$, the same criterion applies, and $N=0$ works.
